newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore shares end down on row and data woes.
newsitem.headline: Singapore shares end down on row and data woes.

text.p: Singapore shares closed down on Thursday depressed by a diplomatic row with Malaysia and the impact of worse-than-expected economic numbers, dealers said.
"The row is the news of the day. It's kept people out of the market and given them an excuse to sell," said a local dealer.
The benchmark Straits Times Industrials Index (STII) ended down 23.06 at 2,154.33, off 1.06 percent from Wednesday's close.
But the row over Senior Minister Lee Kuan Yew's description of Johor as "notorious for shootings, muggings and car-jackings" in a sworn affidavit was expected to blow over.
"What's really interesting are the figures," another dealer said after news on Wednesday January's industrial output fell 7.2 percent year on year, causing worry about economic recovery.
In a day of concerted selling, losers outnumbered gainers by 311 to 81 on traded share volume of 229 million units.
Losers were led by Creative Technology, down Singapore $0.70 at S$14.80, but it was motor retailer Cycle & Carriage which had most negative impact on the STII, losing S$0.60 to S$14.10.
North Borneo Timbers, Genting Berhad, Berjaya Leisure and Malayan Banking, all Malaysian shares traded over the counter in Singapore, were the top gainers. REUTER
